question: What was the average claim cost at each Chicago repair shop in 2025?

input.sql: select repair_shop_id,name,state,metro,network_status from repair_shops where metro ilike '%chicago%'

WITH source AS (
    SELECT c.*, p.channel, p.metro,
           coalesce(pay.paid, 0) AS paid_to_date,
           coalesce(pay.paid, 0) + c.reserve_amount AS incurred,
           c.close_date - c.report_date AS days_to_close
    FROM claims c
    JOIN policies p USING (policy_id)
    LEFT JOIN (
        SELECT claim_id, sum(amount) AS paid FROM claim_payments GROUP BY claim_id
    ) pay USING (claim_id)
)
SELECT repair_shop_id, sum(incurred) / count(*) AS value
FROM source
WHERE loss_date >= DATE '2025-01-01'
  AND loss_date <= DATE '2025-12-31'
  AND repair_shop_id IN ('RS-037', 'RS-039', 'RS-041')
GROUP BY ALL
ORDER BY ALL

report.interpretation: Average claim cost (incurred = paid + open reserve, divided by claim count, by loss date) for claims at the three repair shops in Chicago (IL), for loss dates 2025-01-01 to 2025-12-31. I used the agreed average_claim_cost metric. Repair shops are only set on auto collision, glass and hail claims.
report.answer: 2025 average claim cost by Chicago shop: Valdez Auto Body (RS-037, preferred) $2,475 over 48 claims; Reid Collision Center (RS-039, preferred) $3,525 over 47 claims; Campbell Body Works (RS-041, non-preferred) $4,301 over 29 claims. Campbell is the highest, about 74% above Valdez. It is the only non-preferred shop, so it has no agreed rates. Its claims are spread across all adjusters and channels, so I found no single adjuster or channel driving the gap. Samples are small (29 to 48 claims), so treat the gap as a signal for review, not a verdict.
